newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Taiwan's China Synthetic closer to Malaysia plant.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan's China Synthetic closer to Malaysia plant.

text.p: Taiwan's China Synthetic Rubber Corp is in the final stages of negotiations with partners to build a U.S.$70 million carbon black plant in Malaysia, company president Peter Wu said on Monday.

He did not specify the partners, but the company said last month it had entered into a draft agreement with U.S. affiliate Continental Carbon Co and NC Resources Group of Malaysia to work on the project.
The worldscale plant would have production capacity of 75,000 tonnes a year and start production in about two years, Wu told reporters on the sidelines of a chemicals conference in Singapore.
"I hope to have the plant ready in about two years," he said.

The plant would be built on the west cost of Malaysia, north of the capital Kuala Lumpur and output would be geared to both domestic sales and exports. Carbon black is used to make tyres and rubber products.
Wu said the company was still interested in building a plant in China but it would not be a worldscale plant.
"Nothing is concrete," he said of the company's China ambitions.
The company's spokesman Shao Chung said in January plans to build a carbon black plant in China had been put on hold, indicating the project had fallen victim to frictions between Taipei and Beijing.
China Synthetic also has plans to expand into South America and Europe, Wu said on Monday.
